outline.chapter_title: Introduction to Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning and Orthogonal Constraints
outline.description: This chapter establishes the context of large foundation models, the necessity of efficient adaptation, and introduces the core concepts of Orthogonal Fine-Tuning (OFT). It contrasts OFT with other methods like LoRA and identifies the specific parameter-efficiency bottleneck in standard OFT that motivates this research.
subtopics: The challenge of training foundation models from scratch vs. fine-tuning
Overview of Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) paradigms: Full fine-tuning, Adapter tuning, Prompt tuning
The principle of preserving pretraining knowledge: Pairwise angles and spectral norms
Introduction to Orthogonal Fine-Tuning (OFT): Multiplicative updates and angle preservation
Limitations of standard OFT: High dimensionality of dense orthogonal matrices ($\mathcal{O}(d^2)$)
The block-diagonal compromise in OFT: Sparsity patterns, inductive biases, and expressivity trade-offs

outline.chapter_title: An Information Transmission Framework for Matrix Factorization
outline.description: This chapter presents the novel theoretical perspective proposed in the paper: viewing the construction of a dense orthogonal matrix as an information transmission problem on a grid graph. It explains how matrix factorization corresponds to sequential information exchange between nodes.
subtopics: Reframing dense matrix generation as information flow on a $d \times (m+1)$ grid graph
Mapping matrix elements to directed edges: Zero entries as blocked paths
Desiderata for efficient factorization: Dense connectivity vs. minimum free edges
The role of orthogonality constraints on graph topology (bijection requirements)
Visualizing sparsity patterns through induced graphs
Comparing naive dense connections ($\mathcal{O}(d^2)$) vs. factorized sparse connections

outline.chapter_title: Butterfly Structures and Efficient Orthogonal Parameterization
outline.description: This chapter details the core technical contribution: using butterfly structures inspired by the Cooley-Tukey FFT algorithm to construct dense orthogonal matrices with $\mathcal{O}(d \log d)$ parameters. It covers the mathematical definitions and recursive construction of these matrices.
subtopics: The Cooley-Tukey Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) algorithm as a source of inspiration
Definition of Butterfly Factors ($\bm{B}^F(k)$) and Butterfly Components ($\tilde{\bm{B}}(d,k)$)
Recursive construction of $d$-dimensional Butterfly Matrices ($\bm{B}(d)$)
Ensuring orthogonality in butterfly components via Cayley parameterization and 2D rotations
Generalizing to Block Butterfly Components ($\tilde{\bm{B}}^b(d,k)$) for flexibility
Parameter complexity analysis: From $\mathcal{O}(d^2)$ to $\mathcal{O}(d \log d)$

outline.description: This chapter synthesizes the theoretical framework into a practical fine-tuning method called BOFT. It explains the forward pass, initialization strategies, regularization techniques specific to multiplicative updates, and how BOFT subsumes previous methods.
subtopics: Formal definition of BOFT($m$, $b$): Parameters controlling depth and block size
The forward pass equation: Composing multiple orthogonal butterfly components
$BOFT(1, b)$ as Block-Diagonal OFT and $BOFT(1, d)$ as full OFT (Special cases)
$BOFT(\log d, 2)$ for generating dense orthogonal matrices efficiently
Identity initialization strategy for zero-initialization behavior in multiplicative updates
Multiplicative Dropout: Designing regularization for butterfly components instead of additive weights
